chunks: And it is narrated from Dāwūd ibn Sirḥān, who said:
I was in al-Madīnah during the month of Ramaḍān, so I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: 'I want to perform iʿtikāf, so what should I say, and what should I make obligatory upon myself?'
He said: 'Do not leave the mosque except for a necessary need, and do not sit under shades until you return to your place.'

key_terms.أَعْتَكِفَ: to perform iʿtikāf, spiritual retreat in the mosque
key_terms.أَفْرِضُ: to make binding or obligatory upon oneself
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: the mosque, the place of iʿtikāf
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramaḍān, the time in which this iʿtikāf took place
key_terms.مَجْلِسِكَ: your sitting place or designated place in the mosque

ai.seo_question: What are the basic restrictions for leaving the mosque during iʿtikāf?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal instruction regarding iʿtikāf during the month of Ramaḍān. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that the one in iʿtikāf should not leave the mosque except for an unavoidable need and should not sit under shade outside until returning to his place.
